reason: அத்தி is attested both as elephant and as one of the ten nadis (hastijihva), but the only cited verse, 1658 (அத்தி வரைவாடி), is unclear and its reading uses neither the nadi sense nor any clear sense; no cited verse supports the second sense.

குளிகை as the alchemist's pill is traditional, but 'the retained breath or seed' is not an attested reading of the word; in 2305 the pill of flight to Sathuragiri is a plain physical claim and the breath reading is the proposer's.
Lotus and yogic centre are both traditional senses, and in 1857 சிரமதிற் கமலம், the lotus in the head, fairly reads as the crown centre.

ய as the soul is traditional (Tirumanthiram 975: யகாரம் உயிர்), but the cited reading of 1389 (வட்டம்இட்ட யவ்விலே) treats ய as a letter in a drawn yantra and does not apply the soul sense, so no cited verse uses the second sense.
Meru as the spine (merudanda) is traditional, and in 1405 தாகமேரு நாடி fairly names a spinal channel beside மூல நாடி.
ம as malam or maya is traditional Siddhanta letter-doctrine, and 1656 states it outright (மகார மாயையடி ... மலமது).
'Sky-channel' is not an attested compound; it is a pun made by hearing விண்நாடி (seeking the sky) as one word, and the cited reading itself says the plain sense stands without it.

Source and root centre are both traditional senses of மூலம். In 1863 பர மூலநிலைகண்டு fairly admits the root-state reading in a yogic herdsman's song; in 1646 (மூல மானதல்லால் முத்தி அல்லவடி) the root-centre reading is stretched.

கலை as art and as a phase of the breath or digit of the moon (இடகலை, பிங்கலை, சந்திரகலை) are both traditional; in 2302 எழுகலை மறந்து, set among the forgetting of thought and self, the breath-phase reading is fair though low in confidence.
வெளி as open space and as the supreme space (பரவெளி) are both traditional, and 2298 and 2300 (பராபர வெளி, சுத்தப் பரவெளி) fix the second sense.
தாள் is foot and also door-bolt in the lexicons, and the three knots as bolts on the central channel are a traditional yogic sense; 1393 (கதவுதாள் திறந்து) and 1404 (மூன்று தாள்திறந்து) support it.
செப்பு 'to speak' and செப்பு 'copper' are homonyms, not a traditional double reading, and 2314's செப்புக் குயமானார் is obscure; the alchemist reading is a conjecture the verse does not support.

Fire and the fire raised from the root are both traditional, and 1395 and 1405 (மூலநாடி தன்னில்வன்னி மூட்டி, மூல நாடியில் அனல்எழுப்பி) fix the yogic sense; 1394 depends on the unclear சமருவி and is stretched.
Ganapati as the presiding deity of the triangle at the root centre is traditional, and 2293's திரிகோணக் குஞ்சரம், after the Mother and the flawless flame, fairly reads that way.
'Earth' is not an attested sense of பூரி, and the in-breath reading depends on taking பூரியிட்ட as பூரகம், which 1391's obscure line does not fix; the double reading is the proposer's.

Both senses (tantric killing rite, alchemical killing of a metal) are traditional, but in 1650 மாரணம் rhymes with காரணம் in a cosmogonic list and reads most naturally as destruction or death; nothing there supports the alchemical sense.

ரசம் as mercury and as essence or bliss-nectar are both traditional; in 2309 the ரசபான போதை drunk on the path once given to Uma fairly reads as the inner nectar of bliss. The mercury reading of the same line is weak.
மெய் as truth and as body are both standard senses, and in 1645 (விந்து நாதமடி மெய்யாக வந்ததடி) the body reading is fair. 1858's reading uses only the truth sense, so it does not test the entry.

The numeral எட்டு written as அ is a known Siddhar cipher, but neither cited verse is read that way: 1389's readings are breath counts or yantra cells and 1398's says the text gives no key. No cited verse supports the second sense.
அ as the first arising and as the soul are traditional (AUM cosmogony; Tirumanthiram 975), and 1655 (அகாரம் இத்தனையும் அங்கென்று எழுந்தது) fairly supports it; 1390's சீயில்அவ்வில் is stretched.
The nine openings of the body are a traditional sense of the number, named in 2317 (ஒன்பது வாசல்) and fairly applied to 301's nine-torn rag (நான்முழத் தொன்பது பீற்றத் துண்டம்).

தந்தி is elephant (dantin) and also cord or sinew (tantri), so a body's channel is a fair traditional extension; in 1404 தந்தி ஏறிடில், mounted before the nectar descends, reads fairly as the channel.

நடு as the middle and as the central channel (நடுநாடி) are both traditional; in 1409 நடுவறிந்து, set against the root and crown that Mal and Ayan sought, the channel reading is fair though low in confidence.
முச்சுடர் is the standard name for sun, moon and fire, and their reading as the two breaths and the root fire is traditional; 2307 places it right after மூலாதாரம், which supports it.
Root channel and சுழுமுனை are traditionally identified, and 1395, 1403, 1405 and 1413 all fairly read as the central channel; the two senses are close, a specification rather than a true double.
கடல் as the heart or self is not an attested traditional reading; 1397's நமதுகடலில் is more likely a misprint for நமது உடலில், which gives the plain sense 'in our body'.
Head and crown centre are both traditional, and 1857's சிரமதிற் கமலம் fairly reads as the crown; the two senses are close.
The inner tirtha is a traditional Siddhar and yogic relocation of the temple bath, and 1407 states it (ஆதி சக்கிரத்தினில் அமர்ந்துதீர்த்தம் ஆடுவன்).
Door and bodily opening or crown aperture are both traditional; 2317 (ஒன்பது வாசல்) and 1406 (மேலை வாசல்) support the second sense, while the three doors of 1393 are less certain.
This is a textual emendation (கவனக் for கமனக்), not a word read in two senses; 2305 does not use 'attention' at all, so there is no double reading to record.
Highway is plain, and 'great path' (mahapatha) is a traditional name of the sushumna; in 2317, after the nine doors are shut, மேலாம் பெருவழி ஊடுசென்று fairly reads as the central channel.
Water and the nectar from above are both traditional in yogic texts, and 1395's அந்த நீருண after the root fire fairly reads as nectar; 1394 rests on the unclear சமருவி.
Foot and step (one of the four paths) are both plain senses, and 1395, 1401 and 1646 (நாலுபாதம்) use the step sense fairly.
வாதம் has both senses in Tamil, but the only cited verse, 301, has the humour fixed by பித்தம் and கோழை beside it, and no cited verse supports the alchemy sense.
Nectar of the gods and the yogic nectar of the crown are both traditional, and 1404 (அமுதம்வந்து இறங்கிடும் after the ascent) fairly supports the second.
Emptiness and the void as the Supreme are both traditional, and 1860 (சூனியமானத்தைச் சுட்டுவார் எங்குண்டு ... புத்தி சூக்குமம்) treats the void as the goal.
Circle and the three bodily regions of sun, moon and fire are both traditional, and 1651 (மாறாத மண்டலமும் வந்தது மூன்று) fairly supports the second; 1404's single மண்டலம் is less certain.
Horse and breath-as-practice are both traditional, and 1396 (வாசிவானில் ஏறி) and 1397 (வாசியை நடத்திடில்) fairly read as the breath.
சி as Siva in the five syllables is traditional, and 1656 (சிகார மூலம்) states it; 1390's சீயில்அவ்வில், paired with அ as soul, is stretched.
